title: Skills, Plugins and HermesContextBus
summary: Extending Hermes safely, including shared context

lessons.title: Skills vs plugins
lessons.body: Skills are pointer-based procedures; plugins are code with hooks. Nerve is a plugin; your procedures are skills.

lessons.title: HermesContextBus
lessons.body: An opt-in shared-context layer: typed records with origin, trust scope, per-profile isolation, redaction, bounded retention, and fail-closed behavior when the bus is down.

lessons.title: Isolation rules
lessons.body: Profile A publishes to authorized profile B; profile C cannot read across scope. The bus never gains execution authority.

lab.goal: Publish a synthetic record from profile A and read it from authorized profile B; confirm C cannot.
steps: Install the bus: packages/hermes-context-bus (see its README).
Enable shared_context for two sandbox profiles only.
Run the exchange check: python3 -m hermes_nerve.integrations.shared_context --demo
Attempt an unauthorized scope read and confirm rejection.
lab.expect: You can describe the trust scope triplet (origin, profile, project).

task.intro: Answer the scenario questions; the engine verifies them deterministically in a disposable fixture. Your answers are never executed as commands.

questions.q: Which admission states does Selective Context use? (pin/admit/defer/suppress)
questions.why: PIN/ADMIT/DEFER/SUPPRESS gate memory, tools and skills.

questions.q: May profile C read a message addressed to profile B? (yes/no)
questions.why: Cross-profile reads are denied without authorization.

questions.q: What happens to Nerve core when the bus is down? (crash/fallback)
questions.why: A disabled/unavailable bus falls back safely; core is unaffected.

executable.task: Produce a shared-context exchange plan with explicit authorization boundaries.

check.question: Q: What happens to Nerve core when the bus is unavailable?
expected_keywords: nothing - core runs normally (fail-closed bus, fail-open core)

troubleshooting: No provider or network call happens merely by enabling the profile UI.
The bus never holds execution policy or task lifecycle authority.
